sn55.24:1.2: He appears only in this Sutta and the next. MS spells his name saraṇāni. Pali names often have different spellings. Unless there is a reason otherwise, I adopt the choices by Bodhi, who, following the most common international practice, usually follows the Sinhalese manuscripts.
sn55.24:1.11: Drinking alcohol violates the fifth precept, meaning that he could not be a stream-enterer. It is noteworthy that this Sutta follows immediately after one where the key question is whether keeping precepts is essential for a stream-enterer.
sn55.24:9.7: Saddhāmatta (“a degree of faith”) is sufficient for one to progress in the path (MN 22:47.2, MN 70:21.2). Compare saddhāmattaka, which is used in a diminutive sense, “mere faith” (MN 65:28.5, AN 6.55:11.2).
sn55.24:9.11: Sarakāni was not a “drunk stream-enterer”, as slandered by the Sakyans. Here he is said to have completed the factors of stream-entry by undertaking the training (in the five precepts) on his deathbed (see SN 55.28:2.7), while SN 55.21:1.13 confirms that he “fulfilled” said training.
